title: Disable SysMain (Superfetch)
description: Stop the service that preloads frequently used apps into RAM.
danger: On hard drives this can make app launches and boot noticeably slower. On SSDs the gain is usually small. Easy to revert.
why: Can reduce background disk/CPU use on some systems, but usually helps on HDDs and can slow app launches. Mostly pointless on fast SSDs; measure before keeping it.

title: Remove startup app delay
description: Launch your startup apps right away instead of waiting a few seconds.
why: After sign-in Windows deliberately waits before starting your startup apps. Setting the delay to zero removes that pause.

title: Faster menus
description: Open menus instantly instead of after a short pause.

title: Disable window animations
description: Skip the minimize and maximize animations.
why: Windows animates windows when they minimize or maximize. Turning this off makes the desktop feel a little snappier. Takes effect after signing out.

title: Stop apps running in the background
description: Prevent Store apps from working while closed.
why: Many Store apps keep running after you close them, using CPU, RAM and battery.
danger: Apps stop updating and sending notifications while closed. Chat apps from the Store may miss messages until you open them.

title: Disable Windows Search indexing
description: Stop the background indexer that scans your files.
why: The indexer keeps a database of your files so searches are fast, at the cost of background disk and CPU use.
danger: Start menu and Explorer searches get slower, and apps that rely on the index (such as Outlook search) may stop finding things.
